football_evidence.question: Can Utah State hold Colorado State to field goals?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Utah State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 0.6 of the 3.6 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Utah State has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Utah State’s offense averages 6.5 yards per pass attempt, and Colorado State’s defense allows 11.5 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).

When Utah State has the ball (third down): Utah State’s offense converts 32.3% of its third downs, and Colorado State’s defense allows opponents to convert 60.6% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When Utah State has the ball (big plays through the air): Utah State’s offense turns 7.0% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Colorado State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 18.4% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Utah State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Utah State’s offense turns 6.3% of its runs into explosive gains, and Colorado State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 13.0% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).
contradicting: When Utah State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Utah State’s offense has allowed a sack on 8.6% of its dropbacks, and Colorado State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 5.1% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Colorado State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Colorado State’s offense has allowed a sack on 1.1% of its dropbacks, and Utah State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 4.3% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).

When Colorado State has the ball (third down): Colorado State’s offense converts 49.3% of its third downs, and Utah State’s defense allows opponents to convert 41.6% of their third downs (FBS average 39.5%).

When Colorado State has the ball (the red zone): Colorado State’s offense succeeds on 63.4% of its red-zone plays, and Utah State’s defense allows success on 32.1% of opponent red-zone plays (FBS average 43.6%).
